test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In a two stroke petrol engine, during the upward stroke of the piston, the gases are compressed in the piston, and at the same time, which of the following is also performed during the operation?

options.text: Exhaust gases enter the crank chamber through the valve.
Fresh air and fuel (petrol) mixture enters the crank chamber through the valve.
Fresh fuel enters in the cylinder from the crank chamber through the valve.
Fresh air for petrol engine enters the cylinder from the chamber through the valve exhaust port.

solution:
The correct answer is __Fresh air and fuel (petrol) mixture enters the crank chamber through the valve**.**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Two-stroke petrol engines__ operate with a simplified mechanism compared to four-stroke engines.
 
• During the upward stroke of the piston, the gases in the cylinder are compressed for ignition.
 
• Simultaneously, the fresh air-fuel mixture enters the crank chamber through the inlet valve.
 
• This process ensures the engine is ready for the next cycle of combustion and power generation.
 
• The absence of separate intake and exhaust strokes in a two-stroke engine increases efficiency but may lead to greater wear and tear.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Two-stroke Engine:**

 
 
• A two-stroke engine completes a power cycle in just two strokes of the piston (one revolution of the crankshaft).
 
• It combines the intake, compression, power, and exhaust processes into two movements of the piston.
 
 
 
• **Four-stroke Engine:**
 
 
• In contrast, a four-stroke engine requires four strokes of the piston (two revolutions of the crankshaft) to complete one power cycle.
 
• This design separates the intake, compression, power, and exhaust processes into distinct strokes.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Two-stroke engines are commonly found in lightweight applications such as motorcycles, chainsaws, and small boats.
 
• Four-stroke engines are widely used in cars, trucks, and other heavy-duty applications due to their durability and fuel efficiency.
